cohort: 3028 women at risk of haemorrhage undergoing caesarean section
finding: Routine use of cell salvage during caesarean section had a modest effect on reducing donor blood transfusion rates, but this was associated with increased fetomaternal haemorrhage in RhD-negative women with RhD-positive babies and was not considered cost-effective.
mod_finding: The study investigated the effects of routine cell salvage use during cesarean section on blood transfusion rates and maternal morbidity.
